### `ecommerce_mall_administrator_grades`

Tracks administrator grade changes including promotions and demotions
with complete audit trail.

This subsidiary table records every grade change event for
administrators, maintaining a chronological history of grade transitions.
Each record captures the grade after the change, the previous grade
before the change, and who made the modification. The table enforces one
grade change per administrator per timestamp through a composite unique
constraint.

The {changedBy} field tracks which administrator initiated the grade
change (can be the administrator themselves for self-promotion requests,
or another super administrator for approval-based changes). The
{administrator} field references the target administrator whose grade is
being changed.

{\@link ecommerce_mall_administrators} is the parent entity managing all
administrator accounts on the platform.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key for this administrator grade change record.
- `administrator_id`
  > References the administrator whose grade is being changed.
  >
  > This foreign key establishes the 1:N relationship where one administrator
  > can have multiple grade change records over their career. The
  > administrator entity ({\@link ecommerce_mall_administrators}) is the
  > parent in this relationship.
- `changed_by`
  > References the administrator who initiated this grade change.
  >
  > This is typically a super administrator who has promotion/demotion
  > authority. Can be the same administrator for self-promotion requests, or
  > a different super administrator for approval-based grade changes. The
  > referenced administrator must have sufficient grade level to make the
  > change.
- `grade`
  > The new grade after this change was applied.
  >
  > Allowed values: 'regular' (standard administrator), 'super' (super
  > administrator with elevated permissions including admin management). This
  > represents the administrator's grade after the change event was
  > completed.
- `previous_grade`
  > The grade before this change was applied.
  >
  > Can be null for the initial grade assignment when an administrator
  > account is first created. Otherwise contains the previous grade value
  > ('regular' or 'super') before the change.
- `reason`
  > Optional reason for this grade change.
  >
  > Can be used to document business justifications for promotions,
  > demotions, or administrative overrides. Left null when no specific reason
  > is provided.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this grade change record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this record was soft deleted. Null if still active.

### `ecommerce_mall_administrator_grades_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of administrator grade changes for audit trail.

This table captures immutable records of when an administrator's grade is
changed (promoted or demoted). Each snapshot preserves the old grade
value and the new grade value at the moment of change, along with
timestamps.

Snapshots are immutable audit records that cannot be modified once
created. They support historical tracking of grade transitions and enable
auditing of who received what grade change and when. Deleted snapshots
are soft-deleted to preserve historical reference.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ecommerce_mall_administrator_grade_id`
  > Reference to the administrator grade record that was changed.
  >
  > This foreign key establishes a many-to-one relationship with the parent
  > administrator grade record. Each snapshot is tied to a specific grade
  > change event for a particular administrator grade record.
- `old_grade`
  > The grade value before the change.
  >
  > This field captures the administrator's previous grade (e.g., 'regular'
  > or 'super') immediately prior to the grade transition.
- `new_grade`
  > The grade value after the change.
  >
  > This field captures the administrator's new grade (e.g., 'regular' or
  > 'super') immediately after the grade transition.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created.
  >
  > This marks the exact point in time when the grade change occurred.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp for this snapshot.
  >
  > Null indicates the snapshot is still active. A non-null value indicates
  > the snapshot has been soft-deleted.

### `ecommerce_mall_administrator_approval_requests`

Tracks user requests to become platform administrators, requiring super
administrator review and approval.

### Purpose
Captures when a user (customer or seller) submits a request to become an
administrator, including their reason and the review outcome. Maintains
complete audit trail of admin approval workflow.

### Workflow
- Users submit requests with reason for seeking admin status
- Super administrators review pending requests
- Approved requests result in new administrator account creation
- Rejected requests remain in system for audit purposes

### Status Flow
- pending → approved (becomes administrator)
- pending → rejected (request denied)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `requesting_member_id`
  > References the member (customer) requesting admin status. NULL if
  > requester is a seller.
  >
  > This field creates a one-to-many relationship where one member can have
  > multiple approval requests in different statuses.
- `requesting_seller_id`
  > References the seller requesting admin status. NULL if requester is a
  > member.
  >
  > This field creates a one-to-many relationship where one seller can have
  > multiple approval requests in different statuses.
- `reviewing_super_admin_id`
  > References the super administrator who reviewed this request.
  >
  > NULL for pending requests, set when a super admin approves or rejects the
  > request.
- `created_admin_id`
  > References the administrator account created when request was approved.
  >
  > NULL for pending or rejected requests. Contains the ID of the new
  > administrator record created upon approval.
- `status`
  > Current status of the approval request.
  >
  > - pending: Request submitted, awaiting review
  > - approved: Request approved, admin account created
  > - rejected: Request denied by super administrator
- `reason`
  > Reason provided by user for requesting administrator status.
  >
  > User explains why they believe they should have admin privileges. Used by
  > super administrators to evaluate the request.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the approval request was submitted.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was last updated (status change or
  > modification).
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the request was soft deleted. NULL means request is active.

### `ecommerce_mall_administrator_approval_requests_snapshots`

Immutable audit trail snapshots capturing point-in-time states of
administrator approval requests.

Each snapshot is created when an administrator approval request is
created, approved, or rejected. Snapshots preserve the complete state at
that moment for compliance and dispute resolution purposes. These
snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted once created.

See: [ecommerce_mall_administrator_approval_requests](#ecommerce_mall_administrator_approval_requests)

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key identifier for each snapshot record.
- `ecommerce_mall_administrator_approval_request_id`
  > Foreign key reference to the original administrator approval request
  > being snapshot.
  >
  > Establishes the relationship between this snapshot and its source
  > approval request. Each snapshot is tied to exactly one approval request,
  > and an approval request may have multiple snapshots over its lifecycle
  > (created, approved, rejected).
- `reviewed_by_administrator_id`
  > Foreign key reference to the super administrator who reviewed and made a
  > decision on the approval request (if the request was approved or
  > rejected).
  >
  > Nullable because snapshots may be created before a decision is made
  > (pending status). When status is 'approved' or 'rejected', this field
  > will contain the super administrator's ID.
- `requester_id`
  > Identifier of the user requesting administrator access.
  >
  > This is a polymorphic reference: the actual user type is determined by
  > requester_type field. When requester_type is 'member', this references an
  > ecommerce_mall_member. When 'seller', it references an
  > ecommerce_mall_seller.
- `requester_type`
  > Type classification of the requester (user seeking administrator access).
  >
  > Allowed values: 'member' (customer requesting admin access), 'seller'
  > (seller requesting admin access). This field enables polymorphic
  > referencing to the requester without needing separate FK fields for each
  > actor type.
- `request_reason`
  > The reason provided by the requester for wanting administrator access.
  >
  > This text captures the requester's justification for admin privileges and
  > is preserved in snapshots to maintain historical context of why access
  > was granted or denied.
- `status`
  > Current status of the administrator approval request at the time of
  > snapshot.
  >
  > Allowed values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. This field reflects
  > the decision state when this snapshot was created and is immutable
  > (snapshots are point-in-time records).
- `approved_grade`
  > The administrator grade being approved if the request was approved.
  >
  > Allowed values: 'regular' (standard administrator with limited scope),
  > 'super' (super administrator with full platform control). Nullable when
  > status is 'pending' or 'rejected'.
- `review_reason`
  > Reason provided by the super administrator for approving or rejecting the
  > request.
  >
  > Nullable when status is 'pending'. Contains the administrator's
  > explanation when status is 'approved' or 'rejected'.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created (point-in-time record).
  >
  > Represents the exact moment this state of the approval request was
  > captured for audit purposes. This field is never modified after snapshot
  > creation.

### `ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of seller approval requests capturing status
changes and rejection details for audit trail.

Each snapshot represents a version of a seller approval request at a
specific moment in time, typically created when the request status
changes from pending to approved or rejected. Snapshots preserve the
request reason, reviewer assignment, rejection reason (if applicable),
and other state information at the time of the status transition.

This audit trail enables historical analysis of the approval process,
supports compliance requirements, and allows administrators to review the
progression of seller approval requests. Snapshots are immutable records
that cannot be modified after creation, ensuring data integrity for
regulatory and operational purposes.

The snapshot is linked to the parent {@link
ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_requests} entity through a unique foreign
key, enabling retrieval of the full request history when needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ecommerce_mall_seller_approval_request_id`
  > References the parent seller approval request that this snapshot belongs
  > to.
  >
  > Each snapshot is uniquely associated with one version of a seller
  > approval request. The relationship is 1:1 with a unique constraint,
  > ensuring exactly one snapshot per request version. This foreign key
  > enables efficient retrieval of all snapshots for a given approval request
  > when auditing the approval history.
  >
  > The snapshot captures the state of the request at a point in time,
  > allowing historical analysis of status changes, rejection reasons, and
  > reviewer actions.
- `seller_id`
  > References the seller who submitted the approval request.
  >
  > This field is denormalized from the parent seller_approval_request for
  > query performance, allowing direct access to seller information without
  > joining to the parent table. The seller_id enables reporting on approval
  > metrics by seller and supports queries that need to filter snapshots by
  > seller identity.
- `reviewer_id`
  > References the administrator who reviewed and processed the approval
  > request.
  >
  > Only populated when the request status is approved or rejected. For
  > pending requests, this field is null as no reviewer has been assigned
  > yet. The reviewer_id provides accountability by tracking which
  > administrator made the approval or rejection decision, supporting
  > performance reviews and audit requirements.
- `request_reason`
  > The reason provided by the seller for requesting administrator access.
  >
  > This is the original request reason submitted by the seller when creating
  > the approval request. It captures the seller's motivation and
  > justification for wanting administrative privileges. The reason is
  > preserved in the snapshot to maintain historical context of why the
  > request was made, regardless of the final decision.
- `rejection_reason`
  > The reason provided by the administrator when rejecting a seller approval
  > request.
  >
  > Only populated when the request status is rejected. This field captures
  > the administrator's justification for denying the seller's request to
  > become an administrator. The reason may include missing documentation,
  > policy violations, or other disqualifying factors. For approved or
  > pending requests, this field is null.
- `status`
  > The approval request status at the time this snapshot was created.
  >
  > The status can be one of the following values:
  > - "pending": The request has been submitted but not yet reviewed by an
  > administrator
  > - "approved": The administrator has approved the request and the seller
  > has been promoted to administrator
  > - "rejected": The administrator has rejected the request with a provided
  > rejection reason
  >
  > The status field enables filtering snapshots by approval state and
  > tracking the progression of requests through the approval workflow.
- `created_at`
  > The timestamp when this snapshot was created.
  >
  > This timestamp represents the point in time when the snapshot was
  > generated, typically coinciding with a status change event on the parent
  > approval request. The created_at field enables chronological ordering of
  > snapshots and supports temporal queries that need to retrieve the state
  > of an approval request at a specific time.
- `updated_at`
  > The timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated.
  >
  > For snapshots, this field typically remains unchanged as snapshots are
  > intended to be immutable audit records. However, the field is maintained
  > for consistency with the temporal field requirements across all business
  > entities.
- `deleted_at`
  > The timestamp when this snapshot was soft deleted, if applicable.
  >
  > Snapshots are typically preserved for compliance and audit purposes, so
  > deletion is rare. If soft deletion is enabled, this field records when
  > the snapshot was marked for deletion. Null indicates the snapshot is
  > active and in use.

### `ecommerce_mall_categories_snapshots`

Immutable point-in-time records of category modifications for audit trail.

Captures the complete state of categories whenever administrators make
changes, including name, description, parent assignment, or any other
attribute. Each record is immutable once created, providing a complete
history of category evolution.

This table supports compliance requirements and enables reviewing
historical category states. Snapshots are created on every modification
to the referenced categories.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key for category snapshot record.
- `category_id`
  > Reference to the category that was modified.
  >
  > Maintains referential integrity with the source ecommerce_mall_categories
  > record.
- `parent_category_id`
  > Reference to the parent category in the snapshot state.
  >
  > Captures the parent-child relationship at modification time. May be null
  > if the category has no parent at that time.
- `modified_by_id`
  > Reference to the administrator who made the modification.
  >
  > Identifies which admin user triggered this snapshot for accountability
  > and audit purposes.
- `entity_type`
  > Type identifier for the snapshot target entity.
  >
  > Always set to 'category' to distinguish snapshot type.
- `entity_id`
  > The ID of the category at the time of snapshot creation.
  >
  > Matches the category_id for internal consistency.
- `name`
  > Category name as it existed at the time of modification.
  >
  > Preserved value when the snapshot was created.
- `description`
  > Category description as it existed at the time of modification.
  >
  > Preserved value when the snapshot was created.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the snapshot was created.
  >
  > Represents the exact point in time for this immutable record.

### `ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions`

Records seller suspensions and unsuspensions performed by administrators
for platform oversight.

This table tracks when sellers are suspended or unsuspended, including
the reason for suspension and timestamps for when actions occurred. Each
suspension record is immutable and preserved as part of the audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`
  > References the seller who is being suspended or unsuspended.
  >
  > This FK establishes the relationship between suspension records and
  > seller entities. A single seller may have multiple suspension records in
  > the audit trail if they are suspended and unsuspended multiple times.
- `suspended_by_admin_id`
  > References the administrator who performed the suspension or unsuspension
  > action.
  >
  > This FK tracks which administrator took the action, providing
  > accountability in the audit trail. The administrator must exist in
  > ecommerce_mall_administrators.
- `suspended_at`
  > Timestamp when the suspension took effect.
  >
  > This marks the beginning of the suspension period. For unsuspensions,
  > this may represent when the previous suspension was resolved, depending
  > on how records are structured.
- `resolved_at`
  > Timestamp when the suspension was resolved (unsettled or unsuspended).
  >
  > Nullable field - if null, the seller is currently suspended. If
  > populated, the seller has been unsuspended.
- `reason`
  > Human-readable explanation for the suspension or unsuspension action.
  >
  > This field captures the reason why the seller was suspended or
  > unsuspended, such as policy violations, customer complaints, or
  > administrative review decisions.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this suspension record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this suspension record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this suspension record was soft-deleted.
  >
  > Nullable field for soft delete support. If null, the record is active.

### `ecommerce_mall_user_bans`

Track bans issued to customers and sellers by administrators with
timestamps and reasons.

This table maintains an audit trail of user bans across both customer and
seller accounts. Each ban record documents when a user was banned, who
issued the ban, and the reason for the ban.

### Purpose

Captures administrative decisions to restrict user access to the
platform. Supports both customer and seller entities through polymorphic
foreign key design with subtype tables.

### Fields

- `id`: Primary key
- `user_type`: Discriminator for customer vs seller
- `administrator_id`: Administrator who issued the ban
- `reason`: Written explanation for the ban
- `banned_at`: Timestamp when ban became effective
- `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`: Temporal fields

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `administrator_id`
  > Administrator who issued the ban.
  >
  > References the administrator responsible for the ban decision, enabling
  > accountability and audit trail for administrative actions.
- `user_type`
  > Discriminator for user type: 'customer' or 'seller'.
  >
  > Determines which subtype table holds the polymorphic reference. Enables
  > single table to track bans for both customer and seller entities.
- `reason`
  > Written explanation for why the user was banned.
  >
  > Required field documenting the business justification for the ban. Used
  > for audit trail and transparency.
- `banned_at`
  > Timestamp when the ban became effective.
  >
  > Marks the exact moment the restriction was applied to the user account.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. NULL means active ban.

### `ecommerce_mall_user_ban_of_customers`

Customer ban subtype that references banned customers in the polymorphic
user ban system.

This table is part of the ban management infrastructure that tracks when
customers are banned from the platform. It maintains a 1:1 relationship
with the main {{ecommerce_mall_user_bans}} table, where the main table
stores ban metadata (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, reason) and this
subtype table stores the specific customer reference.

Bans are created when administrators or super administrators ban
customers for policy violations, and are managed through the main bans
table with this subtype providing customer-specific context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ban_id`
  > References the main ban record in {{ecommerce_mall_user_bans}}. This is a
  > 1:1 relationship ensuring exactly one customer ban subtype per ban
  > record.
  >
  > The unique constraint on this field enforces the 1:1 relationship,
  > preventing multiple subtype records from referencing the same ban.
- `customer_id`
  > References the {{ecommerce_mall_members}} table for the banned customer
  > account.
  >
  > This field identifies which customer account is being banned and is
  > managed exclusively through ban operations from the administrator or
  > super administrator interface.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this ban subtype record was created.
  >
  > This timestamp is typically the same as the parent ban's created_at but
  > is stored here for independent audit queries on customer bans
  > specifically.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this ban subtype record was last modified.
  >
  > For bans, updates typically occur when the ban is lifted (soft delete) or
  > when additional metadata is added.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this ban subtype record was soft deleted (ban lifted).
  >
  > Null value indicates the customer is currently banned. When set,
  > indicates the ban has been removed and the customer account restored.

### `ecommerce_mall_user_ban_of_sellers`

Seller subtype table for polymorphic user ban records, establishing a 1:1
relationship with [ecommerce_mall_user_bans](#ecommerce_mall_user_bans).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ecommerce_mall_user_ban_id`
  > Unique reference to the parent ban record that this seller-specific
  > details augment.
  >
  > Establishes a 1:1 relationship with [ecommerce_mall_user_bans](#ecommerce_mall_user_bans). The
  > unique constraint on this field ensures each seller can only have one
  > active ban at a time.
- `seller_id`
  > Reference to the seller account that is banned.
  >
  > Points to [ecommerce_mall_sellers](#ecommerce_mall_sellers). Tracks which seller account is
  > subject to the ban.
- `created_at`
  > Record creation timestamp.
  >
  > Automatically set when this ban subtype record is created.
- `updated_at`
  > Last update timestamp.
  >
  > Automatically updated on every record modification.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp.
  >
  > Nullable - set when the ban subtype record is logically deleted, allowing
  > for data recovery.

Create comprehensive OpenAPI schemas and TypeScript/NestJS API interfaces for an e-commerce shopping mall platform with the following endpoints and operations:

**Customer Account & Profile:**
- POST /auth/customer/register - Register new customer account
- POST /auth/customer/login - Customer login
- POST /auth/customer/logout - Customer logout
- POST /auth/customer/password/change - Change customer password
- DELETE /auth/customer/account - Delete customer account

**Customer Address:**
- GET /customer/addresses - List customer addresses
- POST /customer/addresses - Add new address
- PATCH /customer/addresses/{id} - Update address
- DELETE /customer/addresses/{id} - Delete address
- PATCH /customer/addresses/{id}/set-default - Set default address

**Seller Account:**
- POST /auth/seller/register - Register new seller account
- POST /auth/seller/login - Seller login
- POST /auth/seller/logout - Seller logout
- POST /auth/seller/password/change - Change seller password
- DELETE /auth/seller/account - Delete seller account (with validation)
- GET /auth/seller/approval-status - Get seller approval status

**Seller Profile:**
- GET /seller/profile - Get seller profile
- PATCH /seller/profile - Update seller profile (creates snapshot)

**Categories:**
- GET /categories - List all categories
- GET /categories/{id} - Get category details
- GET /categories/{id}/products - Get products in category

**Product Search & Listing:**
- GET /products - Search products with filters and sorting
- GET /products/{id} - Get product detail

**Product Management (Seller):**
- POST /seller/products - Create product
- PATCH /seller/products/{id} - Update product (creates snapshot)
- DELETE /seller/products/{id} - Delete product (with validation)
- GET /seller/products - List seller's products

**Product Images (Seller):**
- POST /seller/products/{id}/images - Upload product image
- PATCH /seller/products/{id}/images/{imageId}/reorder - Reorder images
- DELETE /seller/products/{id}/images/{imageId} - Delete product image

**Product Variants (Seller):**
- POST /seller/products/{id}/variants - Add variant
- PATCH /seller/products/{id}/variants/{id} - Update variant (creates snapshot)
- DELETE /seller/products/{id}/variants/{id} - Delete variant (with validation)

**Product Variants (Customer):**
- GET /products/{id}/variants - Get all variants of a product

**Inventory Management (Seller):**
- POST /seller/products/{id}/variants/{variantId}/inventory - Add inventory record
- GET /seller/products/{id}/variants/{variantId}/inventory - Get inventory history

**Wishlist:**
- POST /customer/wishlist - Add product to wishlist
- DELETE /customer/wishlist/{productId} - Remove product from wishlist
- GET /customer/wishlist - List wishlist items (paginated)

**Shopping Cart:**
- POST /customer/cart - Add variant to cart
- PATCH /customer/cart/{cartId} - Update cart item quantity
- DELETE /customer/cart/{cartId} - Remove cart item
- DELETE /customer/cart/products/{productId} - Remove all items of product from cart
- GET /customer/cart - Get cart items

**Checkout & Orders:**
- POST /customer/checkout - Create order from cart
- GET /customer/orders - List customer orders (paginated)
- GET /customer/orders/{id} - Get order details

**Shipping & Tracking:**
- GET /customer/orders/{id}/shipments - Get shipments for order
- POST /customer/shipments/{id}/confirm-delivery - Confirm delivery

**Seller Dashboard:**
- GET /seller/dashboard - Get seller dashboard summary
- GET /seller/order-items - List all order items for seller's products

**Order Cancellation:**
- POST /customer/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/cancel - Request cancellation
- PATCH /seller/order-items/{itemId}/cancel-request - Approve/reject cancellation request
- GET /customer/cancel-requests - List cancellation requests

**Order Refund:**
- POST /customer/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/refund - Request refund
- PATCH /seller/order-items/{itemId}/refund-request - Approve/reject refund request
- GET /customer/refund-requests - List refund requests

**Reviews:**
- POST /customer/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/reviews - Create review
- PATCH /customer/reviews/{id} - Update review (creates snapshot)
- DELETE /customer/reviews/{id} - Delete review
- GET /products/{id}/reviews - Get reviews for product

**Administrator - User Management:**
- POST /admin/users/admin-request - Request admin status
- GET /admin/users/admin-requests - List admin requests
- PATCH /admin/users/admin-requests/{id} - Approve/reject admin request
- PATCH /admin/users/{userId}/admin-grade - Change admin grade
- GET /admin/users/customers - List all customers
- PATCH /admin/users/{customerId}/ban - Ban/unban customer
- GET /admin/users/sellers - List all sellers
- PATCH /admin/users/{sellerId}/ban - Ban/unban seller

**Administrator - Seller Management:**
- GET /admin/sellers/pending - List pending seller registrations
- PATCH /admin/sellers/pending/{id} - Approve/reject seller registration
- PATCH /admin/sellers/{sellerId}/suspend - Suspend/unsuspend seller

**Administrator - Category Management:**
- POST /admin/categories - Create category
- PATCH /admin/categories/{id} - Update category
- DELETE /admin/categories/{id} - Delete category

**Administrator - Product Oversight:**
- GET /admin/products - List all products
- GET /admin/products/{id}/snapshots - Get product snapshots
- DELETE /admin/products/{id} - Delete product (policy violation)

**Administrator - Order Oversight:**
- GET /admin/orders - List all orders
- PATCH /admin/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/force-cancel - Force cancel item
- PATCH /admin/orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/force-refund - Force refund item
- PATCH /admin/orders/{orderId}/force-cancel - Force cancel entire order
- PATCH /admin/orders/{orderId}/force-refund - Force refund entire order

Please generate comprehensive OpenAPI schemas and TypeScript/NestJS code for all these endpoints.

operations.specification: 1. Validate request body fields: fingerprint (required, string). 2. Check if guest with fingerprint exists in ecommerce_mall_guests. 3. If exists, update updated_at timestamp. 4. If new, create guest record with fingerprint, set created_at and updated_at. 5. Create guest session in ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions with: guest_id, ip (from request header), href (from request body), referrer (from request header if present), created_at, expired_at (set to now + 24 hours). 6. Generate JWT access token and refresh token. 7. Store session_id in response. 8. Return 201 for new guest, 200 for existing guest.
operations.description:
Register a new guest user or refresh existing guest session.

Creates a guest account identified by device fingerprint and establishes a browsing session. The fingerprint uniquely identifies the user's browser/device combination without requiring personal information. Sessions include IP address, current page, and referrer for analytics and session tracking.

Guests receive access and refresh tokens for authenticated browsing. The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows token renewal without re-registration. Sessions expire after 24 hours by default.

This operation is required before unauthenticated users can browse the platform. Existing guests are identified by matching fingerprint, allowing session continuation across visits.

requestBody.description: Guest registration and session initiation data

responseBody.description: Authenticated guest session response with tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification: 1. Extract refresh token from request body. 2. Validate token format and decode payload. 3. Check if token is expired by comparing with expired_at stored in session. 4. Verify token hasn't been revoked (check deleted_at on session record). 5. If valid, generate new access token and refresh token with 24-hour expiration. 6. Update session record with new tokens and refresh the expired_at timestamp. 7. Return new tokens in IAuthorized response format.
operations.description:
Renew guest authentication tokens without re-registration.

Allows existing guests to obtain new access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh token. The refresh token is validated against the stored session to ensure it hasn't expired or been revoked. Upon successful validation, new tokens are issued with extended expiration.

This operation maintains guest session continuity without requiring fingerprint re-submission or additional personal information. It enables guests to continue browsing across multiple visits within their 24-hour session window.

Token renewal is required when access tokens expire (short-lived for security) while maintaining the underlying guest account and session record. Invalid or expired refresh tokens will fail validation and require a new join operation.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request with current refresh token

responseBody.description: Refreshed authentication tokens

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Create new member account in ecommerce_mall_members table. Hash password with BCrypt before storage. Create initial email verification record in ecommerce_mall_member_email_verifications with status='pending'. Send verification email with token. Return IAuthorized containing access_token, refresh_token, and expired_at after successful registration and token generation. Validation: email must be unique, password must meet complexity requirements (min 8 chars, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit), display_name optional, phone_number optional format E.164.
operations.description:
Register a new customer account on the e-commerce platform.

Creates a new member account with email and password credentials. The account is created with email verification required before full activation. An email verification token is generated and sent to the provided email address. The account can authenticate immediately but certain features may be restricted until email verification is completed.

The registration process validates email uniqueness against existing accounts in the database. Passwords are hashed using BCrypt with a work factor of 12 for security. After successful registration, JWT tokens are generated and a member session record is created in the ecommerce_mall_member_sessions table.

Related operations: login (authenticate after registration), refresh (obtain new tokens), and the email verification flow handled by backend email service.

requestBody.description: Customer registration data including email, password, and optional profile information.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing JWT tokens and session expiration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate email and password credentials against ecommerce_mall_members table. Find member record by email using @@unique([email]) index. Verify password_hash using BCrypt.compare. On success, create new session in ecommerce_mall_member_sessions with access_token, refresh_token, ip from request header, href and referrer from request headers. Update session expired_at to current time + 1 hour for access token, + 7 days for refresh token. Return IAuthorized with tokens and expiration. On failure: 401 Unauthorized with error message. Edge cases: account deleted (deleted_at not null) should fail with account not active error.
operations.description:
Authenticate a member customer using email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email and password against the stored credentials in the ecommerce_mall_members table. Upon successful authentication, generates JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a session record in the ecommerce_mall_member_sessions table to track the login session.

The access token is valid for 1 hour and must be included in the Authorization header for authenticated API requests. The refresh token is valid for 7 days and can be used to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating. Session metadata including IP address, page URL, and referrer are captured for security auditing and analytics.

Related operations: refresh (obtain new tokens when access token expires), logout (end session by client-side token removal). Note: Logout is a client-side operation only - JWT tokens expire naturally and do not require server-side invalidation.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing JWT tokens and session expiration.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate refresh token from request body against ecommerce_mall_member_sessions table using @@unique([access_token]) index lookup (stored in refresh_token column). Check token expired_at > now. Find corresponding member record. Generate new access_token and refresh_token. Update session record with new tokens and new expired_at. Return IAuthorized with new tokens. On failure: 401 Unauthorized. Edge cases: token not found (invalid/used/expired), session deleted (cascade delete on member deletion), multiple concurrent sessions (each has own refresh token).
operations.description:
Obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh token.

Allows authenticated members to obtain fresh tokens without re-entering credentials. The refresh token is validated against the ecommerce_mall_member_sessions table to ensure it exists, has not expired, and belongs to an active session. Upon validation, new access and refresh tokens are generated and the session record is updated with the new token values.

This token rotation mechanism enhances security by limiting the lifespan of access tokens while maintaining session continuity. The refresh token must be stored securely on the client and sent with each refresh request. Each refresh operation invalidates the old refresh token, preventing replay attacks.

Related operations: login (initial authentication when no tokens exist), join (register new account). Access tokens should be used for all authenticated API requests by including them in the Authorization header.

requestBody.description: Refresh token from previous authentication session.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing new JWT tokens and session expiration.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: 1. Receive registration data: email, password, display_name. 2. Validate email format and uniqueness in ecommerce_mall_sellers table (check deleted_at IS NULL). 3. Validate password complexity (min length requirements). 4. Validate display_name format and uniqueness if required. 5. Hash password with BCrypt (cost factor >= 12). 6. Create new ecommerce_mall_seller record with: email, password_hash (hashed), display_name, approval_status='pending', is_suspended=false. 7. Generate email verification token: create ecommerce_mall_seller_email_verifications record with unique token, token_hash, email, expires_at (24 hours from now), verified=false. 8. Send verification email to provided email address. 9. Return IAuthorized response with access_token and refresh_token from new session. 10. Create ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions record with access_token, refresh_token, ip, href, referrer, expired_at. 11. Return JWT tokens in response. Error handling: 409 Conflict for duplicate email, 400 Bad Request for invalid data format or password too weak, 500 Internal Server Error for system failures.
operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the ecommerce platform.

Creates a new seller account with email and password credentials. The seller must provide a display_name for their public-facing identity. Upon successful registration, the seller receives JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) for authenticated API access. The account starts with approval_status='pending', meaning the seller must wait for administrator approval before they can list products or fulfill orders.

Email verification is required: a verification token is sent to the provided email address. The seller must verify their email to activate the account. The token expires after 24 hours.

The seller's approval status can be checked via the approval-status endpoint. Administrators review pending sellers and either approve them to start selling or reject with a reason.

## Security Considerations

- Passwords are hashed with BCrypt before storage
- Email verification prevents abuse with fake accounts
- Approval workflow ensures platform quality control
- JWT tokens have limited expiration and require refresh
- IP address and referrer are logged for session auditing

requestBody.description: Seller registration data

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and seller info

operations.name: join

operations.specification: 1. Receive login credentials: email and password. 2. Find seller in ecommerce_mall_sellers table by email (check deleted_at IS NULL). 3. Return 404 Not Found if no active seller found with that email. 4. Check if seller is suspended: if is_suspended=true, return 403 Forbidden. 5. Check approval status: if approval_status='pending' or 'rejected', return 403 Forbidden with reason. 6. Verify password: compare provided password with password_hash using BCrypt verification. 7. If password is invalid, return 401 Unauthorized. 8. Create new session: generate access_token and refresh_token JWTs. 9. Create ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions record with tokens, ip, href, referrer, expired_at. 10. If seller has existing active session (deleted_at IS NULL), consider revoking or allowing multiple sessions based on business rules. 11. Return IAuthorized response with new tokens. Error handling: 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials, 403 Forbidden for suspended or unapproved sellers, 404 Not Found for non-existent account, 500 Internal Server Error for system failures.
operations.description:
Authenticate a seller and obtain access tokens.

Validates seller credentials (email and password) against the database. Upon successful authentication, issues new JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) that grant access to authenticated API endpoints. The seller must have approval_status='approved' and is_suspended=false to login.

The session record includes the client IP address, original URL, and referrer for security auditing and session management. Tokens have expiration times and must be refreshed before expiry.

## Authentication Flow

1. Submit email and password in request body
2. System validates credentials against stored password_hash
3. If valid, check account status (not suspended, approved)
4. Generate new JWT tokens for access and refresh
5. Return tokens in response for use in Authorization header

## Security Considerations

- Failed login attempts should be rate-limited to prevent brute force attacks
- Password verification uses secure BCrypt comparison
- Session tracking enables detection of suspicious login activity from different IPs
- Token expiration enforces re-authentication after session timeout

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and seller info

operations.name: login

operations.specification: 1. Extract refresh_token from request body. 2. Find the refresh_token in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions table. 3. Verify token exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL). 4. Check token expiration: verify current time < expired_at. Return 401 Unauthorized if expired. 5. Find the associated seller in ecommerce_mall_sellers table using ecommerce_mall_seller_id from session. 6. Verify seller account is still active (deleted_at IS NULL), not suspended (is_suspended=false), and approved (approval_status='approved'). 7. Generate new access_token and refresh_token JWTs with fresh expiration. 8. Create new session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions with new tokens. 9. Mark old session as deleted (soft delete) for audit trail. 10. Return IAuthorized response with new tokens. Error handling: 401 Unauthorized for invalid/missing/expired tokens, 403 Forbidden if seller account is suspended or deleted, 404 Not Found if session record not found, 500 Internal Server Error for system failures.
operations.description:
Renew expired access tokens using a valid refresh token.

When an access_token expires, sellers can obtain new tokens without re-entering their credentials by using the refresh_token. This operation validates the refresh_token, verifies the seller account is still in good standing, and issues a new pair of JWT tokens.

The refresh token is session-bound and can only be used once. After successful refresh, the old session is marked as deleted to prevent replay attacks. This ensures each session has a unique, non-reusable refresh token.

## Refresh Flow

1. Submit refresh_token in request body
2. System validates token exists and has not expired
3. Verify seller account is still active and approved
4. Generate new access_token and refresh_token
5. Invalidate old session (soft delete)
6. Return new tokens for continued API access

## Security Considerations

- Refresh tokens have limited lifetime for security
- Each refresh invalidates the previous token
- Token rotation prevents token theft from being used indefinitely
- Account status is re-validated to prevent access to suspended/deleted accounts

Register a new seller account on the ecommerce platform.

Creates a new seller account with email and password credentials. The seller must provide a display_name for their public-facing identity. Upon successful registration, the seller receives JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) for authenticated API access. The seller's approval status can be checked via the approval-status endpoint. Administrators review pending sellers and either approve them to start selling or reject with a reason.

- Passwords are hashed with BCrypt before storage
- Email verification prevents abuse with fake accounts
- Approval workflow ensures platform quality control
- JWT tokens have limited expiration and require refresh
- IP address and referrer are logged for session auditing

1. Submit email and password in request body
2. System validates credentials against stored password_hash
3. If valid, check account status (not suspended, approved)
4. Generate new JWT tokens for access and refresh
5. Return tokens in response for use in Authorization header

## Security Considerations

- Failed login attempts should be rate-limited to prevent brute force attacks
- Password verification uses secure BCrypt comparison
- Session tracking enables detection of suspicious login activity from different IPs
- Token expiration enforces re-authentication after session timeout

operations.description:
Renew expired access tokens using a valid refresh token.

When an access_token expires, sellers can obtain new tokens without re-entering their credentials by using the refresh_token. This operation validates the refresh_token, verifies the seller account is still in good standing, and issues a new pair of JWT tokens.

The refresh token is session-bound and can only be used once. After successful refresh, the old session is marked as deleted to prevent replay attacks. This ensures each session has a unique, non-reusable refresh token.

## Refresh Flow

1. Submit refresh_token in request body
2. System validates token exists and has not expired
3. Verify seller account is still active and approved
4. Generate new access_token and refresh_token
5. Invalidate old session (soft delete)
6. Return new tokens for continued API access

## Security Considerations

- Refresh tokens have limited lifetime for security
- Each refresh invalidates the previous token
- Token rotation prevents token theft from being used indefinitely
- Account status is re-validated to prevent access to suspended/deleted accounts

Session records are used to track authenticated user sessions across multiple devices and browsers, enabling features like session management and security auditing.

The session is identified by its UUID-based session ID. Only active, non-expired sessions are returned. Expired sessions (where expired_at has passed) or soft-deleted sessions (where deleted_at is populated) return a 404 Not Found error.

Authentication is required to access session details—users can only view their own sessions. Administrator and super administrator actors can view any session for security and support purposes.

operations.specification:
1. Validate sessionId is a valid UUID format
2. Query session record by ID across the appropriate session table (member/seller/administrator/super_administrator/guest)
3. Determine session type from the session record (check the actor reference)
4. Validate session is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
5. Validate session is not expired (expired_at > current time)
6. If session not found, not expired, or soft-deleted: return 404 Not Found
7. Check authorization:
   - If authenticated user: only return session if the session belongs to the requesting user (actor_id matches authenticated user ID)
   - If admin/super_admin: allow viewing any session (for support/security purposes)
8. Return session details excluding sensitive data (access_token, refresh_token) from the response
9. Include: id, actor_id (type-specific), actor_type (member/seller/administrator/super_administrator/guest), ip, href, referrer, created_at, updated_at, expired_at
10. Do NOT include access_token or refresh_token in the response (security)

Edge cases:
- Session expired but not yet soft-deleted: return 404
- Session belongs to different user without admin privileges: return 403 Forbidden
- Session ID in invalid format: return 400 Bad Request
- Concurrent modification (updated_at changed during query): handle via optimistic locking if applicable

The actual token is delivered via email, not returned in the API response, to prevent token exposure.

If the email is not found in any actor table, the request is accepted anyway to prevent user enumeration attacks.

This endpoint does not require authentication as it's part of the account recovery flow.

2. Validate email format (RFC 5322).
3. Query all actor tables to check if email exists.
4. Determine actor type and use corresponding password reset table.
5. Generate cryptographically secure random token (UUID).
6. Set expires_at to 1 hour from now.
7. Insert new password reset record.
8. Delete any existing unused tokens for this user.
9. Trigger email service to send reset token (async).
10. Return success response (do NOT expose the token).

Error handling:
- Invalid email format: 400 Bad Request
- Database error: 500 Internal Server Error
- Email service error: log and return success

Security:
- Token must be cryptographically secure.
- Token must be hashed before storage.
- Do NOT return the token in API response.
- Do NOT distinguish between existing and non-existing emails.
- Rate limit by IP address.

responseBody.description: Confirmation that the password reset request was accepted. The actual reset token is sent via email and is not returned in this response.

requestBody.description: Email address to send password reset token to. The email must be valid and match an existing account (though the API accepts any email to prevent enumeration).

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific password reset record by its ID for administrative oversight.

This operation returns the complete password reset token record including the associated user account reference, token expiration status, and usage history. Administrators can view password reset requests to monitor account recovery activities and verify security compliance.

The endpoint works across all user types (customer, seller, administrator, super administrator) as password reset records are stored in separate tables indexed by reset ID.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve the password reset record from the appropriate table based on the resetId.

1. Query the password reset record by ID from the password reset tables
2. Load the associated user account (member, seller, administrator, or super administrator) to include in the response
3. Check if the token has been expired (expired_at or expires_at < current time)
4. Check if the token has been used (used_at is not null)
5. Check if the token has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null)
6. Return the complete record with all fields

Error handling:
- Return 404 if the resetId does not exist in any password reset table
- Return 403 if the token has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null)

The response includes:
- id: The password reset record ID
- User reference: The associated user account ID and type
- token: The reset token (masked in admin view for security)
- expires_at: Token expiration timestamp
- used_at: When the token was used, if applicable
- created_at: When the password reset request was created
- deleted_at: When the token was deleted, if applicable

Note: The actual token value should be masked in responses shown to administrators (show first 4 and last 4 characters only) to prevent token leakage.

responseBody.description: The complete password reset record including user account reference, token status, expiration timestamp, and audit trail information.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the password reset record to retrieve.
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
List and search email verification records with filtering and pagination.

This operation provides administrative oversight of customer email verification processes. It returns a paginated list of email verification records with support for filtering by status, email address, customer membership, and date ranges. The endpoint supports cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large datasets.

Filtering capabilities include status (pending, used, expired, archived), date range queries for creation and expiration times, and partial email matching. The response includes verification token metadata, status information, and timestamps for audit purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_member_email_verifications table with the following logic:

1. Apply search filters from request body:
   - status: filter by exact status value (pending, used, expired, archived)
   - email: partial match on email field (case-insensitive LIKE)
   - ecommerce_mall_member_id: exact match on member ID
   - created_at range: filter by creation date range (gte, lte)
   - expired_at range: filter by expiration date range (gte, lte)
   - deleted_at: filter soft-deleted records (null or not null)

2. Implement cursor-based pagination:
   - Use cursor from previous page response for next page navigation
   - Default page size: 20 records, maximum: 100 records
   - Cursor is based on created_at timestamp and id for stable ordering

3. Sort results:
   - Default sort: created_at DESC (newest first)
   - Support custom sort fields: created_at, updated_at, expired_at

4. Return only non-archived records by default (status != 'archived'), unless explicitly requested

5. Join with ecommerce_mall_members table to include display_name and phone_number if requested

6. Validate all filter parameters for proper format and value ranges

7. Handle edge cases:
   - No matching records: return empty array with pagination metadata
   - Invalid cursor: reject with 400 error
   - Invalid status value: reject with 400 error
   - Requested page beyond available data: return empty results

8. Create snapshot record for each verification token creation as per audit requirements

9. Return IPageIEcommerceMallMemberEmailVerification.ISummary with:
   - records: array of email verification summaries
   - cursor: pagination cursor for next page
   - hasNextPage: boolean indicating if more pages exist
   - totalCount: total number of matching records

10. Respect soft delete: exclude records with deleted_at set unless explicitly requested

11. Ensure proper authorization: only administrators with oversight permissions can access this endpoint

responseBody.description: Paginated list of email verification summary records optimized for administrative oversight and audit trail review.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for email verification records including status filters, date ranges, email patterns, member ID filters, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve the details of a specific email verification record by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns complete information about the email verification including the verification status, associated customer email address, creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and whether the token has been used. The verification ID is a UUID that uniquely identifies the verification token within the system.

This operation is typically used by the system or administrators to check the current state of an email verification process, such as verifying that a customer's email has been successfully verified or checking if a verification token has expired.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_member_email_verifications table for the record matching the verificationId.

Return the complete email verification entity if found, including:
- id: the verification record UUID
- ecommerce_mall_member_id: the customer account UUID
- email: the customer email address being verified
- token: the verification token (may be redacted for security)
- status: current verification status ('pending', 'used', 'expired', 'archived')
- created_at: token creation timestamp
- updated_at: last update timestamp
- used_at: timestamp when token was used (null if not yet used)
- expired_at: token expiration timestamp

If no record is found with the provided verificationId, return a 404 Not Found error.

The token value may be redacted in the response if not needed for administrative purposes.

responseBody.description: Complete email verification record including verification status, associated customer information, timestamps, and token metadata.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the email verification record to retrieve.
parameters.name: verificationId

operations.description:
List all shipping addresses for the authenticated customer with pagination and optional filtering.

Returns a paginated collection of the customer's saved shipping addresses. Each address includes recipient details, full address information, and default status. The response supports filtering by default status and search by recipient name or city.

Addresses that are marked as default are clearly indicated in the response. The operation respects soft-deletion and only returns active addresses (where deleted_at is null).
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_customer_addresses table for records belonging to the authenticated customer (filter by ecommerce_mall_member_id from JWT token).

Apply optional filters:
- is_default: filter addresses by default status (true/false)
- recipient_name: partial match search on recipient name (ILIKE)
- city: partial match search on city (ILIKE)

Apply pagination:
- page: 1-based page number (default: 1)
- pageSize: items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

Sort results by created_at descending (newest first) by default, or by recipient_name/city if specified.

Filter out soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL).

Return IPageIEcommerceMallCustomerAddress.ISummary with total count, page info, and list of address summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer shipping addresses optimized for address management UI displays.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for address list including pagination, default status filter, and text search options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific shipping address belonging to the authenticated customer.

This operation returns the complete address entity including recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country, and default status. Only addresses belonging to the authenticated customer are accessible.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_customer_addresses table for a single record matching the provided addressId and customerId.

1. Validate that customerId and addressId are valid UUIDs
2. Verify the address exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
3. Confirm the address belongs to the authenticated customer (ecommerce_mall_member_id = customerId)
4. Return the complete address record including all fields

Error handling:
- 404 if address not found or belongs to different customer
- 404 if address is soft-deleted
- 401/403 if customer is not authenticated or not authorized

responseBody.description: The complete shipping address entity with all fields including recipient information, location details, and default status.

operations.description:
Creates a new shipping address for the authenticated customer.

The customer can add multiple addresses to their account, each storing recipient information and delivery location details. All address fields must contain valid information. If any required field is missing or invalid, the address creation is rejected.

The created address is immediately available for use in future orders. If the customer indicates this should be the default address, any existing default address is updated accordingly.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract authenticated customer ID from JWT session (ecommerce_mall_member_id)
2. Validate all required fields: recipient_name, phone, street, city, state, postal_code, country
3. If is_default is true, find existing address with is_default=true for this customer and set it to false
4. Insert new address record with auto-generated UUID for id, current timestamp for created_at/updated_at, NULL for deleted_at, and the provided is_default value
5. Return the complete address entity including generated id

Error handling:
- Return 400 for missing or invalid required fields (recipient_name, phone, street, city, state, postal_code, country cannot be empty)
- Return 401 if customer is not authenticated

responseBody.description: The created address entity with all fields including the generated unique identifier.

requestBody.description: Address creation data including recipient name, phone number, complete address details, and default flag.

operations.description:
Update an existing shipping address in the customer's address collection.

Modifies the specified shipping address belonging to the authenticated customer. Any of the following fields can be updated: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country, or default status designation.

If the address being updated has is_default=true and another address is set as default, the system will automatically unset the default status from the previous default address to maintain the single-default constraint.

Soft-deleted addresses cannot be updated; attempting to modify a deleted address will result in a not-found error. Addresses must belong to the authenticated customer; cross-customer modifications are not permitted.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update a customer shipping address in ecommerce_mall_customer_addresses table.

1. Find the address by addressId (UUID) with soft-delete check (deleted_at is NULL).
2. Verify ownership: address.ecommerce_mall_member_id must match the authenticated member's ID.
3. Reject if address is soft-deleted (deleted_at is NOT NULL).
4. Reject if address does not exist.
5. Validate request body fields:
   - recipient_name: string, non-empty, max 100 characters
   - phone: string, matches phone format, non-empty
   - street: string, non-empty, max 200 characters
   - city: string, non-empty, max 100 characters
   - state: string, non-empty, max 100 characters
   - postal_code: string, non-empty, max 20 characters
   - country: string, non-empty, max 50 characters
   - is_default: boolean (optional)
6. Handle single-default constraint:
   - If is_default=true in request, set is_default=false for all other addresses owned by this customer.
   - If is_default is not provided, leave existing is_default value unchanged.
7. Update the address with provided fields, set updated_at to current timestamp.
8. Return the updated address object.

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Address does not exist or is soft-deleted.
- 403 Forbidden: Address does not belong to the authenticated customer.
- 400 Bad Request: Invalid field values or format violations.
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Validation constraints violated (e.g., trying to set multiple addresses as default).

responseBody.description: The updated shipping address with all fields including the new values and updated timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipping address to update
parameters.name: addressId

requestBody.description: Updateable fields for the shipping address. Any field not provided will retain its existing value. The is_default field will trigger automatic default reset for other addresses if set to true.

prerequisites.description: Shipping address must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Delete a shipping address from the customer's address collection.

This operation performs a soft delete by marking the address with a deleted_at timestamp, preserving the address data for historical order references while removing it from active address listings. The operation enforces business rules to prevent deletion of addresses currently in use by pending orders and ensures customers maintain at least one address for checkout purposes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated customer owns the address identified by addressId
2. Check for any pending orders (paid, shipped, or cancelled status) that reference this address
   - If address is referenced by pending order, reject with 409 Conflict error
3. Count the customer's remaining active addresses
   - If address is the customer's only address, reject with 409 Conflict error
4. Verify address is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL)
   - If already deleted, reject with 404 Not Found error
5. Set deleted_at to current timestamp for soft delete
6. Update updated_at timestamp
7. Return null response body

Error responses:
- 401 Unauthorized: Customer not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: Customer does not own this address
- 404 Not Found: Address does not exist or already deleted
- 409 Conflict: Address is referenced by pending order OR would leave customer with no addresses
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: Address data is invalid

parameters.description: UUID of the customer shipping address to delete (global scope)
parameters.name: addressId

operations.description:
List all wishlist items for a customer with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities.

Returns a paginated list of wishlists owned by the authenticated customer. Each wishlist item includes product details (name, images, availability status) and indicates whether the wishlist is active or soft-deleted.

The search supports filtering by status (active/soft-deleted), sorting by creation date (ascending/descending), and pagination with cursor-based navigation for large result sets.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_wishlists table with JOIN to ecommerce_mall_products for product details.

Filter criteria:
- customer_id: REQUIRED - filter by authenticated customer's ID (enforce data isolation)
- status: optional - 'active' or 'deleted' to filter by deleted_at null/non-null
- created_after: optional - filter wishlists created after timestamp
- created_before: optional - filter wishlists created before timestamp
- product_id: optional - filter wishlists containing specific product (requires JOIN)
- sort: optional - 'created_at_asc' or 'created_at_desc' (default: created_at_desc)

Implementation:
1. Extract customer_id from JWT token in request headers
2. Build query with WHERE clause: customer_id = {extracted_id}
3. Apply optional filters for status, date ranges, and product_id
4. Perform LEFT JOIN with ecommerce_mall_products on wishlist_items to get product name, images, and availability
5. Check variant stock levels to determine product availability status
6. Apply pagination: limit=20 (fixed), cursor-based navigation for efficiency
7. Return paginated result with next_cursor if more pages exist

Error handling:
- Return 404 if customer_id is missing from token
- Return 400 if invalid sort parameter or invalid status value
- Return 200 OK with empty list if no wishlists found

Edge cases:
- Products in wishlists may have been deleted - filter them out during query
- Soft-deleted wishlists should not be returned unless status='deleted' is specified
- Zero-stock variants should show product as unavailable but remain in wishlist

responseBody.description: Paginated list of wishlist items with product details optimized for customer wishlist browsing.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for wishlist filtering including customer isolation, status filters, date ranges, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single customer wishlist by its identifier, including all wishlist items with product details and availability status.

This operation returns the complete wishlist entity with its associated products. Each item includes product metadata (id, name, images, price, availability status) to enable immediate display without additional API calls. Deleted products are automatically excluded from the result.

**Business Logic**:
- Returns the wishlist with all non-deleted items
- Each item shows current product availability based on variant stock levels
- Automatically excludes products that have been deleted by sellers
- Validates that the wishlist exists and is not soft-deleted
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate wishlistId is a valid UUID format
2. Query ecommerce_mall_wishlists table for record with matching id
3. Verify wishlist.deleted_at IS NULL (active wishlist only)
4. If not found, return 404 Not Found
5. Query ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items for items where ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id matches and deleted_at IS NULL
6. For each item, join with ecommerce_mall_products to get product details
7. Calculate availability status: product is available if any variant has stock > 0
8. Return wishlist with items array containing:
   - Item metadata (created_at, updated_at)
   - Product full details (id, name, images, variants with stock status)
9. Sort items by added date (created_at ascending)

responseBody.description: Full wishlist entity with all items and product details.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the wishlist to retrieve.

operations.description:
Create a new wishlist for the authenticated member customer.

Creates a personal wishlist with the specified name and optional description. The wishlist is associated with the authenticated customer and can store multiple products for later purchase consideration. Optionally, products can be added to the wishlist during creation using the initial_product_ids array.

Only registered members can create wishlists. The system validates that all specified products exist and are currently active before creating the wishlist. Products that have been deleted or deactivated are rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request and extract customer_id from the session token
2. Validate request body:
   - name: required, 1-100 characters
   - description: optional, max 500 characters
   - initial_product_ids: optional array of UUIDs, max 100 items
3. For each initial_product_id, verify the product exists and is not deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
4. Insert new record into ecommerce_mall_wishlists:
   - customer_id: from authentication context
   - name: from request
   - description: from request (nullable)
   - created_at: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
   - updated_at: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
5. For each validated product, insert a record into ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items:
   - ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id: new wishlist id
   - ecommerce_mall_product_id: product id
   - created_at: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
   - updated_at: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
6. Return the created wishlist with associated items

responseBody.description: The created wishlist with its id, name, description, creation timestamp, and list of associated products.

operations.description:
Update an existing wishlist by replacing its editable attributes.

This operation allows a customer to modify their wishlist information. Currently, the only editable field is customer_id, which can be used for data migration or account management scenarios. The updated_at timestamp is automatically modified to reflect the change.

### Security and Validation

- The customer making the request must own the wishlist (customer_id in session must match wishlist customer_id)
- The wishlist must exist and not be soft-deleted
- Customer_id must reference a valid active customer account

### Update Behavior

- This is a full replacement operation
- Only customer_id can be modified
- created_at and id remain unchanged
- Soft-deleted wishlists cannot be updated
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated customer owns the wishlist by comparing session customer_id with wishlist.customer_id
2. Verify the wishlist exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL)
3. Update the customer_id field with the value from request body
4. Set updated_at to the current timestamp
5. Verify the new customer_id references a valid active customer account in ecommerce_mall_members
6. Return the complete updated wishlist entity with all fields
7. Throw 404 error if wishlist not found
8. Throw 403 error if customer does not own the wishlist
9. Throw 400 error if customer_id is invalid or references a soft-deleted customer

responseBody.description: The complete updated wishlist entity with all fields including system-generated timestamps.

parameters.description: The UUID of the wishlist to update
parameters.name: wishlistId

operations.description:
Soft delete a customer wishlist and all its associated items.

Removes a wishlist from active view by setting deleted_at timestamp. All wishlist items are cascade-deleted. Customers cannot access deleted wishlists. The operation is member-scoped — only the wishlist owner can delete it.

**Deletion Behavior**:

- Soft delete via deleted_at timestamp (not permanent removal)
- Cascade delete to all wishlist items
- Products remain intact; only wishlist reference is removed
- Cannot be undone; requires recreation of wishlist and re-adding items
- Deleted wishlists are excluded from all member wishlist queries
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate member and verify ownership of wishlist
2. Find ecommerce_mall_customer_wishlists where id = wishlistId AND ecommerce_mall_member_id = authenticated_member_id
3. If not found or not owner, return 404 Not Found
4. Check if already soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 409 Conflict
5. Begin database transaction
6. Cascade delete all ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items where ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id = wishlistId (defined by ON DELETE CASCADE in schema)
7. Update wishlist: set deleted_at = NOW(), updated_at = NOW()
8. Commit transaction
9. Return deleted wishlist entity with all fields including deleted_at, updated_at, and is_deleted marker

**Error Handling**:
- 404 Not Found: Wishlist not found or not owned by authenticated member
- 409 Conflict: Wishlist already deleted (soft-deleted)
- 401 Unauthorized: Not authenticated

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the wishlist to delete.
parameters.name: wishlistId

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated list of products in a customer's wishlist with filtering and sorting options.

Returns wishlist items with product details (name, main image, available variants) for display in the wishlist view. Items are grouped by wishlist and can be filtered by product name or availability status.

The endpoint supports cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large wishlists. Each page displays the same format with product image, name, price range, and stock status.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items table scoped to the specified wishlistId from path parameter.

Filter conditions:
- WHERE ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id = {wishlistId}
- WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted items)
- Optional: WHERE product name LIKE search term if name_filter provided
- Optional: WHERE product availability status if status_filter provided

Join with ecommerce_mall_products to fetch product details (name, main image, price range, availability).

Sort by created_at (descending) by default, or by name if sort_by=name specified.

Apply pagination: page number and page size from request body, default page_size=20.

Return IPageIEcommerceMallWishlistItem.ISummary for each item with:
- item id, created_at
- product id, name, main image URL
- price range from variants
- availability status

Edge cases:
- If wishlist does not exist: return 404 Not Found
- If user does not own wishlist: return 403 Forbidden (authentication required)
- If wishlist has no items: return empty paginated result with 0 items
- If product was deleted: the item should already be soft-deleted and excluded from results
- If product variant stock is zero: show as unavailable but keep item in wishlist (per requirements)

operations.description:
Retrieve a single wishlist item from a customer's wishlist.

Returns the complete wishlist item record including the referenced product details (name, main image, price), wishlist metadata (name, creation date), and the customer relationship. This operation is scoped to the authenticated customer who owns the wishlist.

The response includes the wishlist item's unique identifier, timestamps for creation and last update, and a reference to the wishlisted product with its current catalog information. Soft-deleted items or wishlists are excluded from results.

**Authorization**: Only the customer who owns the referenced wishlist can retrieve items from it. Unauthorized access attempts return a 404 error to prevent information leakage.

**Error handling**:
- 404 Not Found: Item does not exist, wishlist does not exist, or customer does not own the wishlist
- 401 Unauthorized: Customer is not authenticated
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items table by wishlistId and itemId path parameters.

1. Fetch the wishlist item record where id = itemId AND ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id = wishlistId
2. Join with ecommerce_mall_wishlists to fetch wishlist data (customer reference)
3. Join with ecommerce_mall_products to fetch product data (name, price, images)
4. Validate the authenticated customer owns this wishlist (customer_id match)
5. Return the complete wishlist item with wishlist and product details
6. Return 404 if item not found or customer does not own the wishlist

Business rules:
- Only the wishlist owner (authenticated customer) can retrieve their wishlist items
- The wishlist must be active (deleted_at is NULL)
- The item must be active (deleted_at is NULL)

Edge cases:
- Return 404 if wishlistId does not exist
- Return 404 if itemId does not exist in the specified wishlist
- Return 404 if the authenticated customer does not own the wishlist
- Return 404 if wishlist or item is soft-deleted

responseBody.description: Complete wishlist item entity with referenced wishlist and product details.
